To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) a low EBV viral load in the peripheral blood may be detected in the early stages of a PTLD in a lung transplant; 2) the diagnosis of a PTLD is based on the integration of morphological, immunohistochemical, in situ hybridization and molecular studies; 3) a coexistence of a PTLD with acute cellular rejection in the lung transplant may occur.

(i) EBV PCR in peripheral blood is a sensitive screening tool in transplant patients; however, rare patients with PTLD may have a false-negative test result; (ii) a coexistence of acute rejection and EBV-related PTLD should be taken into account both for diagnosis and therapy.
a possible coexistence of acute cellular rejection with PTLD should be considered both in the diagnosis and treatment of lung transplant recipients.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the importance of a correct diagnosis in a patient with a low EB V viral load.
the importance of the correct diagnosis of acute rejection and PTLD in lung transplant patients with low viral load.
the diagnosis and the possible coexistence of acute cellular rejection with EBV-related PTLD in a pediatric lung graft with low EBV viral load.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
PTLD is a rare but potentially fatal complication after lung transplantation.
PTLD is a rare complication of pediatric lung transplantation, which should be suspected in patients with a low EB viral load and a high clinical suspicion.
the diagnosis of PTLD should be considered even in the presence of a low viral load.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
in this case of a pediatric lung transplant recipient, the final diagnosis was an EBV-related PTLD with a very low EBV DNA level in peripheral blood.
the presence of a low EBV viral load does not exclude the possibility of PTLD in a lung transplant patient.
PTLD is a serious complication in lung transplant recipients.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the presence of PTLD in a lung transplant should be considered in the differential diagnosis of acute rejection.
the diagnosis of PTLD should not be excluded in a patient with a low level of EBV DNA, particularly when the clinical and histological features are suggestive.
the diagnosis of a PTLD should be considered in the presence of a lung transplant with acute cellular rejection, even if EBV DNA blood levels are low.
